title: Adaptive SSE segmentation with semantic-boundary framing and reconnect negotiation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive SSE chunking strategy that breaks streamed model outputs at semantic boundaries (sentence/clause/JSON-object) when possible, includes compact per-chunk metadata to support function/tool calling and structured-output reassembly, and negotiates reconnect checkpoints to allow idempotent resumed streams across proxies and mobile clients.
background: Current SSE implementation uses fixed-size or token-count-based chunks which split logical units (e.g., JSON object, function call payload, or sentence) across frames. This complicates downstream parsers, increases reassembly work on the client, and makes reconnect semantics brittle for tool/function-calling workloads. Multiple incidents in the last quarter (see incident notes) show client-side regressions when structured outputs are fragmented mid-object.
proposal: 1) Add lightweight semantic boundary detection in the server runtime to prefer chunk breaks at natural boundaries: sentence terminators, top-level JSON tokens, function-call delimiters, and response stream markers. 2) Attach a small canonical metadata header to each SSE chunk: incremental sequence number, semantic-type tag (sentence|json|func|raw), boundary-confidence (low|med|high), kv-checkpoint-id (short opaque token). 3) Define a reconnect handshake: client supplies last-received sequence number and checkpoint token; server verifies token and returns a resume offset plus deterministic idempotency hints (e.g., 'replay-from-byte', 'trim-prefix-length'). 4) Add compatibility shims in the API layer to emit legacy framing if clients opt out with Accept-Framing: legacy header. 5) Update SDKs to consume chunk metadata and provide convenience reassembly utilities for function calls and structured-output events.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: improves client parsing, reduces reassembly errors, makes reconnect behavior deterministic for tool-calling.
- Cons: adds slight server CPU for boundary detection and small per-chunk metadata overhead (typically <1% token overhead).
- Compatibility: requires careful rollout to avoid breaking existing clients; must provide opt-out and rolling feature flag.
design_decisions:
- Use a best-effort UTF8-safe semantic detector in the runtime; fall back to token/window split if detection is inconclusive.
- Checkpoint tokens are 128-bit opaque IDs derived from the request + KV state; not user-readable.
- Sequence numbers are per-request monotonic integers starting at 1.
- Boundary-confidence is a 3-level enum; clients should only rely on 'high' for strong guarantees.
- Expose Accept-Framing header to allow client-directed compatibility mode.
acceptance_criteria:
- Server emits semantic metadata headers for >95% of chunks in test corpus.
- SDKs can reconstruct function calls and top-level JSON objects without additional RTT for >99% of test prompts.
- Reconnect tests (simulated network drop) can resume and replay deterministically with no duplicated function-calls in 99% of cases.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy mode reproduces current behavior when Accept-Framing: legacy is set.
- End-to-end perf regression <5% p99 latency overhead for streaming flows in canary.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime flag 'semantic_chunking_v1'. 2) Canary on a small subset of hosted traffic (2%), monitor errors/duplicates for tool-calling customers. 3) Ramp to 25% then 75% pending metrics. 4) Enable SDK opt-in with new client versions; after two weeks of stable metrics, flip default for new connections while preserving legacy header support. 5) Include dedicated note in release notes/upgrade guide.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for semantic detector boundary heuristics.
- Integration tests: simulated model outputs (long JSON, nested function calls, mixed text) validated against expected chunk boundaries and metadata.
- Fault-injection: mid-stream disconnects with randomized byte loss to verify reconnect negotiation and idempotency behavior.
- Performance: load tests with canary model profile to ensure <5% regression in p50/p95 latency.
- Back-compat: end-to-end test with 'Accept-Framing: legacy' and current SDKs.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime: add ChunkAnnotator stage post-tokenize but pre-emit. Keep logic pluggable for future detectors.
- API layer: encode metadata as compact JSON in the SSE 'meta' event or as a prefixed header line (choose header line for lower client parsing friction).
- Storage: checkpoint tokens validated against ephemeral request state (no long-term persistence).
- Logging: add sampling for chunk metadata at info level for first 72 hours of canary to validate heuristics.
- Metrics: chunk_boundary_hit_rate, resume_success_rate, duplicate_funccall_rate.
qa_checklist: Verify metadata emitted for top-100 customer prompts
Run reconnect integration across mobile SDKs
Confirm Accept-Framing header honored on proxy and edge CDN
notes: Initial prototype implemented by Luca in a local branch; latency impact negligible on toy models but needs validation on long-context profiles. We should coordinate with CDN and proxy teams to ensure streaming headers are preserved end-to-end. Consider a short-lived compatibility shim for proxies that strip unknown SSE lines.
